itineraryStops[0].name: Hyeopjae Beach
itineraryStops[0].category: West-coast emerald beach + Biyangdo Island view
itineraryStops[0].description: **Hyeopjae Beach (협재 해수욕장)** is one of **Jeju's Top 3 west-coast beaches** and broadly ranked among the island's overall **Top 10 beaches**, defined by its **distinctive silvery-white sand** — formed from **crushed seashells + coral fragments mixed with fine sand**, producing a luminescence rare on the Korean Peninsula. The beach forms a **9 km shoreline** when paired with its **twin-beach companion Geumneung Beach (immediately south, walkable along the same shore, less crowded)** — the two-beach pairing is one of particularly signature photographic windows. The signature view is **Biyangdo Island (비양도)** — a **1.2-km offshore volcanic island with ~200 permanent residents**, accessible by **20-minute ferry from Hallim Port**. Biyangdo is undergoing **Korea's first carbon-free island certification process**, an environmental policy showcase. The beach's **emerald-turquoise water** comes from the shallow coral-sand seabed, and at **low tide, tidal pools reveal hermit crabs, small shrimp, and juvenile fish** — Biyangdo can appear 'walkable' across the shallow expanse. **Pine forest backdrop (Songlim)** behind the beach offers free camping ground and shaded walking paths. Behind the dunes runs Jeju's most-developed **west-coast café strip** — concentrated cafe + restaurant + boutique architecture catering to domestic tourism. **Sunset behind Biyangdo over emerald water** is the visual signature and particularly premier west-coast sunset framing. **FREE admission**; **lifeguarded swim period July 1 – August 31**; ramp-style **wheelchair access** at multiple beach points; public restrooms + changing rooms + showers + equipment rentals year-round. Adjacent **Hallim Park** (botanical garden + lava caves + folk village, separate ₩10,000 admission, 1.5 km away) is occasionally substituted in winter.

itineraryStops[0].whyOnRoute: **West-coast beach opener — and the natural pre-anchor for Hallim Park.** Three southwest-route reasons Hyeopjae is the morning opener at 09:30. (1) **Geographic pairing with Hallim**: Hyeopjae Beach sits **a 5-minute walk north of Hallim Park's main gate** — pairing them as a single morning duo is the local-operator standard and converts what would otherwise be 'two stops within 1 km' into a coherent Hyeopjae→Hallim arc. Visiting Hyeopjae first preserves a **clean, uncrowded beach morning** before the 10:30 Hallim gate-opening tour-bus rush. (2) **Light timing**: Hyeopjae's signature emerald-turquoise water + silvery-white seashell-sand contrast is most photogenic in the **9:30–10:30 morning window** when the sun is high enough to saturate the colors but the late-morning haze hasn't yet built up off the shoreline. (3) **Biyangdo Island anchor for the day's signature wide-landscape photo**: Biyangdo (1.2 km offshore, ~200 residents) sits as the day's first and only **horizon-island silhouette** — every subsequent stop is inland or coastal-cliff, so locking the Biyangdo wide-shot as the morning's first deliverable gives the day's photo set its required landscape breadth before pivoting into the garden + columnar-cliff + tea-fields close.

itineraryStops[1].name: Hallim Park (Hydrangea Festival)
itineraryStops[1].category: Hydrangea anchor + 9 themed gardens + 2 lava-tube caves
itineraryStops[1].description: **Hallim Park (한림공원, founded 1971)** is the southwest coast's anchor botanical park — a **~99,000 m² (originally 100,000 pyeong / 330,580 sqm) garden complex** that **founder Song Bong-gyu transformed from a sandy wasteland into a green paradise** by importing soil and planting palm seeds across a half-century. The park draws **~1.2 million visitors annually** and organizes its space into **nine themed gardens**: the **Subtropical Botanic Garden**, the **Palm Tree Avenue**, the **Wild Grass and Flower Garden**, the **Hyeopjaegul + Ssangyonggul Caves**, the **Jeju Stone and Bonsai Garden**, the **Jae-Am Folk Village** (Joseon-era stone-walled hanok with on-site Dolharubang Restaurant), the **Bird Garden**, the **Jeju Stone Exhibit Hall**, and the **Water Garden**. Hallim's defining structural decision is its **monthly festival calendar** — **January Daffodil → February Plum Flower → March Tulip → April Cherry Blossom → May Wild Flower / Bougainvillea → **June Hydrangea** → July–September Lotus + Water Lily → October Cosmos / Pink Muhly → November Chrysanthemum → December Camellia** — a 12-month cycle that guarantees a **named active festival every month of the year**. The park's two geological landmarks are **Hyeopjaegul Cave (~200m × 10m × 5m, ~25 million years old)** and **Ssangyonggul Cave (~400m × 6m × 3m, 'Two Dragons')** — both part of the same **17 km lava-tube system** but uniquely classified as **'two-dimensional caves'** because lava-tube walls were later coated with **limestone (calcium carbonate) leached from shells in the soil above**, producing the rare global combination of **lava-tube morphology + limestone stalactites/stalagmites** in a single cave system. Cave temperature holds at **17–18°C year-round**, making them natural summer refuges. The park's guest list reflects its diplomatic stature: former Chinese President Jiang Zemin, former Japanese Prime Minister Nakasone Yasuhiro, former Korean President Kim Dae-jung, former Samsung Chairman Lee Kun-hee, and former Hyundai Group Chairman Chung Ju-yung have all visited.

itineraryStops[1].whyOnRoute: **The day's hydrangea anchor — and the southwest route's identity-defining stop.** Four reasons Hallim is the late-morning anchor at 10:30 with a generous 120-min dwell. (1) **Hydrangea season alignment**: June is the Hallim Park monthly-calendar **Hydrangea Festival month** — Hallim is the first of the day's three hydrangea-coded venues (Hallim morning anchor → Camellia Hill afternoon hydrangea tunnel → Osulloc tea-garden afternoon green tone). (2) **Cave-as-weather-fallback**: the **Hyeopjaegul + Ssangyonggul cave pairing** gives the day a guaranteed **indoor-equivalent refuge** against unpredictable southwest-Jeju June weather (June is Korea's pre-monsoon shoulder; afternoon thundershowers happen ~1 in 4 days). The 17–18°C cave temperature also serves as the day's **mid-morning cool-down** before the warm midday transit. (3) **120-min dwell justification**: Hallim's 9 themed gardens + 2 caves cannot be done meaningfully in less than 90 minutes — the 120-min slot accounts for **slow-walking in the caves** (uneven lava-tube floors), **photo dwell at hydrangea field**, and **typical 5-min queue at the cave entrance** during peak season. (4) **Operational pairing with Hyeopjae**: because Hyeopjae sits 5 min walk away, the morning Hyeopjae→Hallim arc consumes 160 min total but only 5 min of vehicle transit — extracting maximum guest value from the operator's morning fuel budget.

itineraryStops[2].name: Lunch (Southwest Jeju)
itineraryStops[2].description: **Lunch is at a local Jeju-style restaurant in the Hallim / Aewol-tail / Andeok corridor**, selected from a vetted shortlist of family-run establishments that the operator has approved for **English-friendly menus, dietary accommodation (vegetarian + halal-friendly chicken/seafood options on request), and west-coast Jeju specialties** at fair group pricing. Typical lunch options include **galchi-jorim (braised silver hairtail)**, **heuk-dwaeji bulgogi (Jeju black pork bulgogi)**, **mom-guk (Jeju seaweed-pork soup)**, and **bibimbap with seasonal namul**. **Mom-guk in particular is a southwest-Jeju regional specialty** that doesn't appear on east-coast tours. Like the east-route lunch, the exact restaurant is selected the day before based on group size, dietary requests, and kitchen availability — guests are notified at the morning briefing. **Lunch cost is at guests' own expense** (~₩12,000–₩18,000 per person) and is **not included** in the tour fee. Beverages and rice/banchan refills are always included with the meal.

itineraryStops[3].name: Jusangjeolli Cliff & Cheonjeyeon Falls
itineraryStops[3].category: Compound stop — Natural Monument 443 columnar joints + Natural Monument 378 three-tier waterfall
itineraryStops[3].description: **This is a paired stop** combining two of Jungmun's signature Natural Monuments into a single ~75-min walking arc — the operator's standard-practice southwest treatment for two anchors that sit a **7-min drive (~3 km)** apart. Stop A is **Daepo Jusangjeolli Cliff (대포 주상절리, 'Daepo Columnar Joints')** — designated **Natural Monument No. 443 on January 6, 2005** (the most recent Jeju coastal Natural Monument designation), a **1.75 km coastal cliff face of polygonal black basalt columns** formed when **Hallasan-eruption lava cooled rapidly against Pacific seawater ~140,000–250,000 years ago**, fracturing the basalt into **hexagonal and pentagonal columns up to 30–40 m tall**. The site is part of the **Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes UNESCO Global Geopark (2010)**. Wave heights during peak south swells reach **20+ meters** crashing against the column base, producing the iconic Jeju basalt-cliff seascape. Stop B is **Cheonjeyeon Falls (천제연, 'Pond of the Emperor of Heaven')** — designated **Natural Monument No. 378 (1993)** for its rare ecological combination of a three-tier waterfall + dense subtropical-warm-temperate transition forest. The name traces to a **Joseon-era Daoist legend that seven heavenly nymphs (선녀, *seonnyeo*) descended nightly to bathe in the upper pond**. The site's signature visual is **Seonimgyo Bridge (선임교, 'Seven Nymph Bridge')** — a 128-m-long arched footbridge with seven nymph statues facing the upper falls. The **operator's pairing logic**: visiting both as a single 75-min stop preserves the day's Hallim+Camellia+Osulloc floral pacing without splitting it across two transits, and the **Jusangjeolli cliff geology + Cheonjeyeon waterfall+forest layering** gives the southwest route its required **non-floral counterpoint** to the day's three garden anchors.

itineraryStops[3].whyOnRoute: **The day's geological + waterfall counterpoint to the three-garden floral arc.** Three southwest-route reasons this compound stop sits at 13:50. (1) **Geographic necessity**: Jusangjeolli + Cheonjeyeon are both in **Jungmun (~3 km apart)** — either both go in or both stay out. Going in is necessary because they are the **only Natural Monuments on the day's path** (alongside the Black Pig at Hueree on the sister tour) and provide the day's required UNESCO-Geopark anchor. (2) **Pacing counterweight**: without this stop, the southwest tour collapses into a garden-only sequence (Hallim hydrangea → Camellia Hill hydrangea → Osulloc tea) that loses visual variety after stop 2. The columnar cliff seascape + three-tier waterfall gorge give the afternoon the visual palette breadth that makes it a complete 'southwest Jeju day' rather than a flower-only tour. (3) **Compound efficiency**: pairing both as 75-min stop frees up **45+ min** vs. visiting each as separate ~60-min stops — that surplus is what funds Hallim's 120-min anchor dwell + Camellia Hill's afternoon photo time.

itineraryStops[4].name: Camellia Hill (Hydrangea Tunnel)
itineraryStops[4].category: Hydrangea tunnel + 172,000 m² largest camellia arboretum in the East
itineraryStops[4].description: **Camellia Hill (카멜리아힐, Jeju Camellia Arboretum)** is a **172,000 m² botanical garden** in Andeok, **the largest camellia arboretum in the East** by acreage and species count: **6,000 camellia trees representing over 500 species sourced from 80 countries**, accumulated over **30+ years** of curation by founder Yang Jong-mun. The garden's signature is its **year-round flowering calendar**, deliberately engineered so that visiting in any season produces a different color palette: **November–March = camellia peak** (red, pink, white, cream-beige varieties — the garden's namesake season); **March–May = cherry blossoms + tulips + late camellias** layered together in dense color mass; **June–August = hydrangeas** (both outdoor stands and a climate-controlled greenhouse showing year-round display); **September–October = fall foliage + late-season bloomers**. Walking paths thread through themed sections — **European Garden, Korean Native Forest Section, Cherry Blossom Walk, Hydrangea Field** — connected by a winding 2.5-km loop that takes ~60–75 min to complete at a leisurely pace. Notable architectural moment: a **glass greenhouse + gallery + cafe** complex at the entrance, which serves as both indoor weather refuge (the only ~15% indoor portion of the visit) and a tea/coffee dwell space with garden views. **Drama filming credit**: variety show **'EXchange / Transit Love 3' (환승연애)** featured Camellia Hill as the location of Ju-won and Yu-jeong's memorable date scene — a draw for fans of the K-reality genre. **Open 365 days a year**; **no outdoor lighting** means the garden closes at sundown (winter ~17:00, summer ~19:00). Admission: **Adult ₩12,000 / Youth + Senior ₩10,000 / Child (4–11) ₩9,000 / FREE under 3**.

itineraryStops[4].whyOnRoute: **The afternoon's hydrangea-tunnel anchor — and the day's photographic centerpiece.** Three southwest-route reasons Camellia Hill is the afternoon-2 anchor at 15:15. (1) **Hydrangea Tunnel — Korea's earliest blooming hydrangeas**: Camellia Hill houses **Korea's earliest-blooming hydrangeas (early April indoor + outdoor full bloom from June)**, with the **Hydrangea Hall pergola tunnel** as the day's definitive Instagram-anchor photo (giant blue/pink/purple hydrangea balls hanging above a covered walkway). The June 10–25 peak window aligns exactly with this tour's seasonal positioning. (2) **Garden-pacing complementarity**: Camellia Hill's **1.2 km / 0.75-mile walking loop** is gentler than Hallim's 9-themed-garden complexity, making it the day's **photo-immersive low-effort garden** after the morning's higher-density Hallim anchor. The two gardens together build a **garden-pacing arc** (intensive Hallim → relaxed Camellia Hill) that wouldn't work if reversed. (3) **Late-afternoon light**: the 15:15–16:30 window catches the **warm late-afternoon golden light** that flatters the hydrangea pinks and blues (midday flat light desaturates them, same logic as Hueree on the east route). Camellia Hill's signature photographers'-mirror installation also captures golden-hour reflections from this slot. **Sister-route note**: this stop matches the afternoon timing of Hueree on the east route — both sister tours close their hydrangea anchor in late afternoon for matching sun angles.

itineraryStops[5].name: Osulloc Tea Museum & Tea Fields
itineraryStops[5].category: Amorepacific tea-culture flagship + green-tea fields finale
itineraryStops[5].description: **O'Sulloc Tea Museum (오설록 티 뮤지엄, '오설록' meaning 'meeting snow + green')** is the tea-culture flagship of **Amorepacific Corporation** — Korea's largest beauty company. Founder **Suh Sung-whan personally pioneered the project in 1979**, reclaiming volcanic ash farmland on Jeju's Seogwang plateau when conventional wisdom held tea couldn't be grown commercially in Korea. Today the **Seogwang Dawon plantation (서광다원)** is **Korea's largest green-tea field**, producing **~700 tonnes annually** across Amorepacific's three Jeju estates. The museum building **opened 2001** in the plantation's heart and was named to **designboom's Top 10 art museums** for its minimalist green-roofed pavilion-amid-tea-rows design. **FREE admission**, daily **09:00–18:00**, ~**2 million annual visitors**. The visit splits naturally into three segments: **(1) Museum interior** — tea production process, antique tea-ware collection from Tang dynasty (618–907 CE) onward, and rooftop observation deck with panoramic plantation view; **(2) Tea House cafe** — signature **green tea rolling cake (오설록 롤케이크)** and **green tea ice cream** served from the tea-leaf harvest year directly; **(3) Plantation walking paths** — gravel rows between tea bushes, popular for sunset photography at the western edge. **Innisfree Jeju House** (Amorepacific's natural cosmetics brand) is a **5-minute walk** for guests interested in the broader brand ecosystem — also free admission with optional tangerine soap DIY workshop (₩15,000). The museum building itself, designed by Korean architect **Mass Studies (Cho Min-suk)**, takes a deliberately low-profile horizontal form that mirrors the tea-row geometry rather than competing with the agricultural landscape — the architectural deference earning it both the designboom Top 10 listing and ongoing use as a case study in Korean contemporary museum design. Optional add-on: the **Osulloc Tea Class (₩30,000 per person, 60 min, advance booking required)** — guided tea-flight tasting with brewing technique demonstration on Korean ceramics, available daily **10:00–16:00**, English-speaking instruction on Wed/Sat sessions.

itineraryStops[5].whyOnRoute: **The day's tea-culture finale — and the southwest route's signature non-floral close.** Three reasons Osulloc closes the day at 16:45. (1) **Tea-color counterpoint to the day's hydrangea palette**: after 4 garden/cliff stops in varying flower-heavy palettes, Osulloc's **emerald-green tea-field rows + Innisfree Jeju House's white-glass architecture** give the day's photo set its closing color tone — saturated green that contrasts with the morning's hydrangea blues/pinks. (2) **Indoor-finale + restroom-buffer**: Osulloc's tea museum + cafe provide the day's **only indoor late-afternoon stop** — guests can use the museum's tea-tasting + ice-cream + restroom facilities to decompress before the **40-min westbound transit back to Jeju City**. The 60-min dwell is sized exactly to allow tea purchase + ice cream + 1 quick tea-field walk. (3) **Brand-cultural anchor**: Osulloc as the **Amorepacific tea flagship (founded 1979 by founder Suh Sung-whan)** ties the day's tour back to one of Korea's globally-recognized brands — a deliberate brand-cultural close that distinguishes this route from generic 'flower garden tours' and gives the day a clear cultural-economic finale story.

whyTourWorks.routeLogicSections[1].title: Why this is summer-only
whyTourWorks.routeLogicSections[1].items: Hydrangea blooms appear from late May, peak mid-June, and fade by mid-July. Outside this window the bloom stops lose their visual draw.
If your dates fall outside hydrangea season, our West & South year-round route covers the same region with year-round POIs (Hallasan, Osulloc, Aewol).
Camellia Hill is Not Camellia Season
Despite the name, this tour visits Camellia Hill specifically for hydrangea — actual camellias bloom in winter.

June Jeju can hit 30°C+ at midday. Bring sun protection — most stops are outdoor.

staticQuestions[0].question: Is this good for first-time visitors to Jeju?
staticQuestions[0].answer: Yes, if you're visiting during hydrangea season (late May to mid-July, peak mid-June). Outside that window, our West & South year-round route covers the same region with year-round POIs.
staticQuestions[1].question: When exactly is hydrangea season?
staticQuestions[1].answer: Approximately late May to mid-July (peak mid-June), with peak typically in mid-June. We update the booking page with year-specific forecast in early May.
staticQuestions[2].question: What if it rains?
staticQuestions[2].answer: Light rain — we operate (hydrangea actually photographs beautifully in soft rain). Heavy rain — we offer free rescheduling within the season window.
staticQuestions[3].question: Why two hydrangea stops?
staticQuestions[3].answer: Hallim Park is an open festival garden; Camellia Hill is a tunnel format. Same flower, complementary compositions.
staticQuestions[4].question: Is this suitable for children?
staticQuestions[4].answer: Yes, age 6+. Walking is moderate at most stops; hydrangea gardens are family-friendly.
staticQuestions[5].question: Is this ok for seniors?
staticQuestions[5].answer: Yes, mostly easy walking. Cheonjeyeon waterfall path has some stairs — can be skipped while group views Jusangjeolli.
staticQuestions[6].question: Where do you pick up?
staticQuestions[6].answer: Hotel lobby pickup within Jeju City is free. Pickup from Seogwipo, Aewol, or Seongsan adds 70,000 KRW due to extra driving distance.
staticQuestions[7].question: Is lunch included?
staticQuestions[7].answer: Lunch cost is separate. Expect 12,000-18,000 KRW per person.
staticQuestions[8].question: Are admission fees included?
staticQuestions[8].answer: Admissions are not bundled by default. Budget ≈30,000 KRW per person: Hallim Park 15,000, Camellia Hill 10,000, Jusangjeolli 2,000, Cheonjeyeon 2,500, Osulloc free.
staticQuestions[9].question: Is Osulloc included?
staticQuestions[9].answer: Yes — museum entry is free. The tea house is separate (optional purchase).
staticQuestions[10].question: What's the difference vs our West & South year-round route?
staticQuestions[10].answer: Different POIs and seasonality. Our West & South year-round route is year-round and visits Hallasan 1100, Osulloc, and Aewol. This tour is summer-only and adds Hyeopjae, Hallim, Jusangjeolli, Cheonjeyeon, Camellia Hill while keeping Osulloc as the closing stop.

page_sections[4].props.itineraryStops[0]: One of Jeju's most photogenic beaches — emerald water, white sand, and Biyangdo island offshore. Easy morning warm-up before the day's main bloom stops.
Brief context on west coast geology
Opens the day with the lightest stop — sets a relaxed pace before the higher-impact hydrangea sites.
Open 24 hours; managed swim season July–August
Sunset shots with Biyangdo silhouette; turquoise color is most vivid at midday under direct sun
Multiple cafés along beachfront; convenience stores
Combine with Hallim Park (5 min walk); avoid summer weekends for fewer crowds
page_sections[4].props.itineraryStops[1]: Botanical garden complex hosting Jeju's largest hydrangea festival in early summer — multiple themed gardens, a lava cave system on-site, and varied bloom colors.
Photo time at peak bloom areas
Peak hydrangea visual stop. Mid-morning timing gives best light without midday heat.
Mar–May 09:00–18:30; Jun–Aug 09:00–19:00; Sep–Oct 09:00–18:30; Nov–Feb 09:00–17:30 (last admission 1 hour before close)
Adult 15,000 KRW / Teen 10,000 KRW / Child 9,000 KRW (online discount: ≈13,500 / 9,000 / 8,100)
Moderate — 2–3 hours of walking through 9 garden zones; mostly flat
Hydrangea Festival (June) and pink muhly (October) are peak photo seasons; lava caves with stalactite lighting are unique
On-site restaurants, gift shop, cave museum
Last entry 90 minutes before closing; closing time depends on sunset; pair with Hyeopjae Beach (5–10 min walk)
page_sections[4].props.itineraryStops[2]: Local restaurant near Hallim or Daejeong — black pork, abalone porridge, or seasonal seafood. Group reset before afternoon stops.
Midday timing balances the morning bloom stops with the afternoon geology and culture stops.
Lunch cost paid direct, ≈10,000–15,000 KRW typical (Korean local restaurants near route)
Vegetarian options on request — notify the day before.
page_sections[4].props.itineraryStops[3]: UNESCO Geopark columnar basalt cliff at Jusangjeolli paired with the nearby three-tier Cheonjeyeon waterfall. Two adjacent UNESCO-recognized geological sites.
Adds geological depth and a clear UNESCO narrative anchor in the southwest part of the day.
Jusangjeolli: Adult 2,000 / Child 1,000. Cheonjeyeon: Adult 2,500 / Child 1,350. Combined ≈4,500 KRW per adult.
Easy — flat wooden boardwalk along cliff; total walk 15–20 min
Best with high tide and rough seas — waves smashing into the columns make dramatic shots; golden hour gives best column-color contrast
Get there before 11am or after 4pm to avoid tour-bus crowds; combine with Jungmun Saekdal Beach (5 min) for a half-day
Small geological exhibition near entrance; souvenir shop
page_sections[4].props.itineraryStops[4]: Botanical garden best known for its dense hydrangea tunnel — a long path lined with massive blue, purple, and pink blooms forming a tunnel canopy.
Camellia and rose garden zones (off-season for camellias)
Second hydrangea peak — the tunnel format is visually distinct from Hallim's open garden bloom field.
Adult 10,000 KRW / Teen 8,000 KRW / Child 7,000 KRW (approximate)
Easy to moderate — gentle hill paths; mostly stroller-accessible
Available at entrance and within garden
Hydrangea tunnel in June; pink muhly grass field in October; camellia varieties peak Nov–Apr
Visit before 10am or after 4pm in peak season to avoid crowds; pair with Osulloc (10 min drive)
Indoor greenhouse café, gift shop, picnic areas
